rv.q: But the drama is beached by its own welter of facts and its experimental switches in form.
BÉZNǍ Theatre helps in the process of chipping away at the silence preferred by Israel and the UK government on The First Year (of the Gaza Genocide in the Media).
BÉZNĂ Theatre presents a blistering multimedia investigation into the relationship between mainstream media, public opinion, and state crime.
More a dramatised essay than a cogent theatrical experience, this remains largely a journalistic rather than a dramatic experience.
It is therefore a sobering and moving experience.
It remains a daring and necessary piece of work.
The First Year (of the Gaza Genocide in the Media) is an essential watch.
Sincere and well-designed but ultimately falls flat.
The four performances are powerful and passionate.
But witnessing is not necessarily theatre.
The First Year (of the Gaza Genocide in the Media) snaps at your attention, during a time when more and more distraction is designed to lure us away.

cn.t: A bold multimedia examination of media coverage during the Gaza genocide earns praise for its fearless political intent and design, but critics find the execution uneven, with form-switching and fact-delivery often overwhelming the material's gravity.
